rationale: Start with a broad, high-strength scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the overall retention window without risking truncation. This gives a balanced first look at spacing across the chromatogram before narrowing or steepening in later injections.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only way to improve CRF is to reduce t_last. Keep composition range and temperature fixed and shorten the gradient to see if elution compresses earlier while resolution remains above 1.5.

We are very close to the optimum: the current run is fully resolved and only 0.51 min above the no-penalty limit, with the critical pair still at R = 1.59. Shorten the gradient one more step to try to pull t_last under 10 min while checking whether the worst pair falls below 1.5.

At 14 min the only loss is the critical 6/7 pair, while time is already ideal. Lower phi1 one step to slightly weaken the late gradient and restore spacing for that pair, aiming to recover full resolution while keeping t_last under 10 min.

The lower phi1 improved the same critical pair while keeping the last peak under 10 min, so continue one more step in that direction. This tests whether the 6/7 pair can reach full credit at essentially no time penalty.

The best tradeoff so far is at phi1 0.90, tG 14, where only the 6/7 pair is slightly under-resolved. Dropping temperature one step should selectively increase retention and often improve selectivity enough to lift that pair above 1.5, while the current t_last has enough room to stay near or just under 10 min.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity badly, so test the opposite direction from the current best method. Raising T one step may shift selectivity favorably for the critical mid-eluting cluster while also trimming retention, giving a chance at full resolution with t_last still under 10 min.

Temperature changes worsened selectivity, so return to 40 C and make the gradient slightly shallower from the current best method. This should improve the 6/7 spacing enough to reach full credit, and the expected small increase in t_last may still beat or match the current best CRF.

The optimum appears to lie near phi1 0.90 and tG 14, with the tradeoff set by one critical mid-cluster pair. Raising phi0 one step while keeping the endpoint fixed compresses the early part of the gradient and changes the slope profile differently than changing tG or T, which may improve selectivity in that cluster without pushing t_last past 10 min.

Injection 9 is very close to ideal, with only the 6/7 pair slightly below 1.5 and comfortable time margin. Lower phi1 one step should further open that critical pair, and the small rise in t_last may still stay under 10 min or remain worthwhile.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so now probe for a more efficient equally optimal method. Raising phi0 one step at the current optimum should shorten the run while likely preserving the well-resolved late region; if all pairs remain at or above 1.5 and t_last stays within 10 min, it is another robust optimum.

The current method still has comfortable margin on the limiting pair and the last peak is under 10 min, so increase phi0 again to seek an even faster equally optimal condition. This continues the boundary search for the strongest starting composition that preserves full resolution.

Phi0 0.15, phi1 0.85, tG 14 is fully optimal with some margin on the critical pair, so shorten tG to test whether a faster gradient can still keep all pairs at or above 1.5. This is the most direct way to look for a shorter equally optimal method around the current best region.

At phi0 0.15 and tG 14, the method is fully optimal with modest margin on the critical 6/7 pair. Lowering phi1 one step should increase spacing for that pair while t_last is already safely under 10 min, testing whether this gives a more robust 1.000 method.

We already have two 1.000 methods, so the goal now is to map robustness around the optimum. Testing a +5 C change from the stronger of the two best methods checks whether full resolution is maintained with an even shorter retention window.

Higher temperature sharply reduced the critical 6/7 resolution, so add back selectivity by making the gradient shallower while keeping the same composition window. This tests whether a longer tG can rescue full resolution at 45 C and define whether temperature can be traded for gradient time.

Since higher temperature was strongly unfavorable, test the opposite side with a shallower gradient to see whether lower temperature can maintain or improve the fully resolved optimum. This maps robustness of the best composition window and could reveal another 1.000 condition if selectivity shifts favorably.

The best space is clearly around 40 C and phi1 0.85, with phi0 0.10–0.15 giving full resolution at tG 14. Testing phi0 0.10 with a slightly shallower 16 min gradient checks for a more robust all-pairs-resolved method and helps define the local optimum plateau around the known 1.000 conditions.

Two exact-optimum methods have been found at phi1 0.85, and the main remaining uncertainty is how wide that optimum plateau is in composition space. Testing phi0 0.15 with a slightly stronger endpoint probes the upper boundary near the best region while keeping all other successful settings fixed.

The best 1.000 method at phi0 0.10, phi1 0.85 sits exactly on the time boundary, while lowering phi1 improved the critical pair in the phi0 0.15 case. Testing phi0 0.10 with phi1 0.80 checks whether that combination can preserve full resolution and pull t_last safely below 10 min, giving a more robust optimum.

A remaining gap is whether the known 1.000 optimum at phi0 0.15, phi1 0.85, tG 14 is robust to a lower temperature without changing gradient slope. This directly isolates the temperature effect at the best composition window and may reveal an alternative optimum or confirm that 40 C is the selectivity sweet spot.

The lower-temperature runs consistently change the identity of the critical pair, but we have not yet isolated that effect at the other 1.000 composition window. Testing this gives the last useful temperature comparison around the second optimum and confirms whether both best methods share the same narrow temperature dependence.

With only three injections left and 1.000 already achieved, the most useful remaining test is a final boundary check for a shorter optimum near the best composition family. Phi0 0.10, phi1 0.90 at 14 min was very close, so shortening tG there determines whether a faster high-endpoint variant can still stay competitive or clearly fails on the same critical pair.

One exact-optimum method remains untested at higher temperature, and with only two injections left the most informative use is to complete robustness mapping around the known best family. This directly checks whether the phi0 0.10 optimum is any less temperature-sensitive than the phi0 0.15 optimum.

For the final run, probe the last untested high-endpoint boundary adjacent to the best region. This completes the local map around the known optima and tests whether a stronger endpoint can still keep t_last below 10 min while preserving near-baseline resolution of the critical pair.
